name: Charlton House

dates.altered: 'Additions 1659 for Sir William Ducie.' The register's Details record that the house was in use as a Community Centre when the entry was written.
dates.note: The register prints a single year, 1612. Wikipedia's article, read by search, gives a construction span of 1607 to 1612 and the Royal Greenwich Heritage Trust's own news page gives 1607. The register's single year is what this record states; the span is recorded here and not merged into it.

quotes.text: (The house is at present a Community Centre). Large Jacobean mansion, built 1612 for Sir Adam Newton. Additions 1659 for Sir William Ducie. The mansion - 3 storeys with H-shaped plan. Red brick with stone dressings and stone bands at floor levels and mullion windows.
quotes.page: Official list entry, Details. The entry is in the legacy continuous-prose format, which carries no MATERIALS/PLAN/EXTERIOR headings and no page numbering; this is the span the first extract returned.

quotes.text: West front has pierced stone parapet. In the centre is a brick and stone projection containing richly ornamented porch and 2 bay windows above with 2-window links to projecting wings of 3 storey bays. East front similar in outline to West and less ornamental in character. North and South elevations 3 storeys 7 windows with square central towers of 5 storeys

note: Tranche 3, 5 Sep 2026, and a NEW exemplar: the node's four existing exemplars are all great country houses, and Charlton is the compact suburban H-plan version of the same vocabulary, now inside London. Extracted twice; the second pass returned only the page furniture and the Open Government Licence line, so the survey rests on one span and is shorter than the others in this cluster. Line breaks collapsed to single spaces. It supports jacobean.c03 as plainly as any record here -- 'Red brick with stone dressings and stone bands at floor levels and mullion windows' -- and it supports the node's porch rule: 'a brick and stone projection containing richly ornamented porch and 2 bay windows above', a porch with rooms over it. Three sources give three build dates and two patrons; all three are in dates.note and none is preferred.
